Commentary.Commentary: We are back for England's first innings. The umpires and the players of Pakistan are out in the middle. As expected, Ben Duckett has not come out to open and it will be skipper Ollie Pope who will join Zak Crawley at the top of the order for England. Shaheen Afridi has the brand-new cherry in hand and is raring to go. Three slips and a gully in place, let's go...
... SECOND INNINGS ...

Right then, the game was getting away quickly from England as Day 2 went on but they have managed to pick up the last two wickets in succession but it is still a tall ask for them with the bat. If Ben Duckett doesn't open then they will have to improvise and make sure that they see the final session on Day 2 through. Join us in a bit as England's reply is up next.

Pakistan are right where they would have liked to be at the end of their first innings. A huge total on the board and more than enough time left in the final session to attack with the new ball. Day 2 though belonged to Salman Agha who's stellar ton to along with the other two centuries we saw on Day 1, has put Pakistan on top of things and their bowlers will be raring to go.

A bizarre 10 or so minutes towards the end of the first innings and Pakistan have managed to put on a massive 556 runs on the board. Abrar Ahmed handed a couple of chances to England which were missed and eventually, when he did fall it was at the expense of Ben Duckett suffering a possible dislocation of the left thumb. He is supposed to open the innings for England which seems highly unlikely now.

OUT! CAUGHT! Finally, England have bowled out Pakistan after 149 overs. Root flattens the trajectory and quickens the pace of the ball, and angles it across the batter like a bumper. Abrar Ahmed is hurried into the shot as he arches back and looks to guide it down to deep third but it bounces a bit more. Abrar is late to slash it and it goes off the higher part and straight to Ben Duckett at the first slip who is quick to react and takes a very sharp catch by stretching his hands in the direction of the ball. Duckett though immediately signals to the dressing room and looks in huge discomfort. He probably has dislocated his left thumb. Pakistan end their first innings on 556.

... DAY 2, SESSION 3 ...

England, on the other hand, had another long session in the field where they had to endure a bit in the first hour with Salman Agha in full flow. However, they did mange to pick up a couple of quick wickets after the drinks break and it looked like they had a chance of finishing off the tail. However, they failed to bowl more deliveries at Shaheen Afridi as Salman frustrated them with his play. They will now look to come back out and pick up the remaining two wickets at the earliest. Join us at 10.02 am GMT for the final session on Day 2.

A session that belonged to one man - Salman Agha made his intentions clear right after the Lunch break, picking up 10 runs in the first over of the session and kept attacking from one end as Saud Shakeel hung around and trudged to his fifty. They did lose a couple of wickets in a short span of time but Salman once again took matters into his own hands and managed to score freely but also retain strike for the new over almost perfectly. Shaheen Afridi too hit a couple of lusty blows and gave ample support to Salman with his running between the wickets.

TEA BREAK, DAY 2! SESSION SUMMARY - 26 overs, 118 runs and 2 wickets. A hugely productive session for Pakistan after Lunch and they have easily piled on 500-plus runs with a couple of wickets still intact. There might be a decision to be made during the Tea break reading declaration whether it comes straight after Tea or sometime during the final session remains to be seen.
Goes full does Gus Atkinson, on middle and leg, Shaheen Afridi tilts ahead and clips it to mid-wicket. And that will be TEA ON DAY 2!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Oh, that would have been one of the catches of the entire year but Chris Woakes was just a millisecond or so early and it will be a six. Tossed up on middle, Salman Agha steps out and looks to go straight down the ground but ends up slicing up high and towards the long off fence. Woakes there backtracks and completes the catch but his momentum is taking him over. He lobs the ball back up, does a 360 over the ropes and then leaps back up to complete the catch. However, the replays from behind the fence show that his right leg was just in contact with the ground when he made contact with the ball again and Salman will be a relieved man.

Commentary.Commentary: Has Woakes managed to catch it cleanly? A tremendous effort by him at long off. He times his jump well and manages to reverse-cup the ball over his head. But loses the balance and goes behind the ropes with the momentum. Flicks the ball back into the field of play, gains his balance, and completes the catch. Although, the TV umpire checks whether he has executed the job cleanly. And to his and England's disappointment, it is deemed that Woakes' right leg was in contact with the ground while the ball was in his hand. He cleanly lifts his left leg in the air but is just milliseconds late to do that with the right leg. This is what the TV umpire thinks here. Hence, NOT OUT! The English players are visibly not happy with the decision, but Woakes had to get nearly everything spot on. Salman Agha was already walking back to the hut but survives eventually. Margin of milliseconds there. Tough luck for England, who have bowled 116 overs now. It will surely be a matter of debate in the cricketing circles as from one angle, it looked like a clean catch, but the benefit of the doubt goes with the batter.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the post-Lunch session, folks! Sun shines in full glory over Multan as the players walk out to the field. English players, after a small team talk spread out to their respective fielding positions. Saud Shakeel unbeaten on 67, and Salman Agha to resume their innings for Pakistan. Jack Leach (26-5-79-2) will bowl the first over of the second session with a slip and a silly point in place. Let's play...
... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

Well then, the first session of Day 2 has flown by. Pakistan still looks in control here as they are nearing the 400 mark. But, England would be pleased as they saw the back of Mohammad Rizwan on a duck, who could have proved to be a resilient customer on the pitch. Although, they have their task cut out and still have four wickets to claim. Saud Shakeel stands unbeaten on 67 and would aim to extend his inning further. Will England come hard on the opposition? Or can Pakistan breach above 450? Do join us for a riveting post-Lunch session after 40 minutes.

England, for their part, had a disappointing initial hour. The seamers found little assistance from the pitch, and their deliveries were met with cautious defense. Shoaib Bashir managed to extract some turn with his spin, but England remained unable to secure that elusive first wicket of the day on a batting-friendly surface. Just as it seemed England had exhausted their plans, Brydon Carse broke through, claiming his maiden Test wicket and ending the team's wicketless drought. And as they say, one brings two, Jack Leach too chipped in with a pricy wicket towards the end of the session.

Building on their strong start from day one, Pakistan continued to assert their dominance. Saud Shakeel and nightwatchman Naseem Shah skillfully navigated the crucial first hour, steadily accumulating runs. Shakeel reached a milestone, notching his seventh Test half-century, while Naseem displayed remarkable resilience too. The latter even managed to clear the ropes a few times, surpassing his previous best score of 18. Their 64-run partnership proved to be a source of frustration for the English attack. Although they lost two quick wickets, and notably, Mohammad Rizwan who was expected to build on another partnership with Shakeel, couldn't even trouble the scorers.

LUNCH, DAY 2 - Session Summary - 26 overs, 69 runs, 2 wickets. A pretty much mixed session but England would be fairly satisfied as they walk into the sheds. It was a slow, sedate, and monotonous first hour of the day, to be fair and it became increasingly evident that the pitch heavily favored the batters. It looked like the session was going Pakistan's way as England's bowlers toiled and sweated relentlessly for breakthroughs. But the second half of the first session brought some delight for the tourists as they managed to claim two in a quick interval.

Right then, the stage is set for Pakistan to pile on more than 500 runs but with the second new ball in play, we might just see England attack a bit more. With the likes of Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Agha still to come, it should be a good contest between bat and ball. Stay tuned as Day 2 action isn't far away.

England will not be too displeased with how Day 1 ended as they managed to pick up 3 wickets in that final session bringing about a bit of relief. They will now look to target the first session in order to make a dent in the Pakistani middle order but they need to be careful as it is still a very flat pitch.

Pakistan piled on 328 runs on Day thanks to a huge stand between skipper Shan Masood and opener Abdullah Shafique with both notching up tons and the former even went on to breach the 150-run mark. On Day 2, they will begin with a well set Saud Shakeel and the night watchman but they still have batting to come.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of this first Test match between Pakistan and England in Multan. If Day 1 is anything to go by, we are in for another run-fest but we might just see a bit more in it for the bowlers as well, who knows.
... DAY 2, SESSION 1 ...

As the Multan pitch remains batter-friendly, Pakistan will look to build on their solid start and push towards a commanding total on Day 2. With Saud Shakeel still at the crease, along with capable batters to follow, the hosts have an opportunity to further stretch their lead. England, on the other hand, will need early wickets in the morning to wrestle back some momentum and prevent Pakistan from running away with the game. Do join us on 8th October for Day 2. The action will begin at 5 am GMT. But as you'll know you can join us early for the build-up. ADIOS!

Abdullah Shafique is up for a chat. He says that performing for the team is a next-level feeling for him. He also praises the way Shan Masood batted with him to build a solid partnership and have put up the performance. He reckons that he worked on his flaws and it's a part of a process to make mistakes and rectify them at the same time. Ends up saying that the cramp he had was nothing but a part of a game and he is doing very well now.

After their dismissals, Babar Azam and Saud Shakeel steadied the ship, stitching a 61-run partnership that kept Pakistan in the ascendancy. Babar, in particular, looked in good touch, guiding his side towards a solid score. However, just before Stumps, England clawed their way back with a crucial wicket, as Azam was caught by Chris Woakes, who made good use of the second new ball. That late breakthrough gave England a glimmer of hope, but Pakistan remains in control, thanks to their formidable top-order display. It was Gus Atkinson who picked up the first wicket after the Tea break. Jack Leach also applied good pressure with three maiden overs on the trot, and got rewarded with a wicket.

SESSION SUMMARY - 34 overs, 95 runs and 3 wickets. It’s been a day dominated by Pakistan’s batters, with the hosts sitting comfortably at 341/4 at the close of play. Resuming at 122/1, Pakistan added to England’s frustration as Abdullah Shafique and skipper Shan Masood piled on the runs in a 253-run partnership. Masood led from the front, reaching 150, while Shafique brought up a well-deserved century. However, both batters, visibly struggling with fatigue in the hot and sunny conditions, fell soon after reaching their milestones. Despite looking uncomfortable, they chose to continue after Tea rather than retiring injured, which ultimately cost Pakistan two quick wickets.

England has toiled hard! They have had their moments with an early wicket of Saim Ayub, but since then, it has been all Pakistan! The pitch is a flatter one though which makes it a batter's paradise.

Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the second session of Day 1. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Shan Masood and Abdullah Shafique will resume their innings. Brydon Carse will start with the ball. Let's play...
... DAY1, SESSION 2...

Right then, England have been handed a taste of their own medicine with how Pakistan have batted in the first session and the home side will now look to consolidate after the break. The visitors will have to attack early and be smart in order to pick up some scalps and get back in the contest. There's still a long way to go on Day 1 but the second session could be crucial for either side. Join us at 7.40 am GMT for the post-Lunch session.

England on the other hand began with some control as Chris Woakes and Gus Atkinson bowled tight lines and the latter picked up a wicket as well. However, they weren't consistent with their lengths and the change-up bowlers gave away some loose balls. Shoaib Bashir was on the receiving end of some attacking cricket from Masood and England will look to employ more of their senior spinner, Jack Leach after the break.

Pakistan walked out to bat on a pitch that looked quite flat but Saim Ayub got strangled down the leg side to hand the opposition an early wicket. However, skipper Shan Masood then walked in and showed positive intent right from the start. Abdullah Shafique too looked solid and the duo piled on runs for fun with both surpassing the fifty-run mark before the Lunch break.

A fine first session from Pakistan's point of view and they have done justice to the captain's decision to bat first. England are seemingly in for a long day in the outfield but as we have seen in Pakistan, wickets do tend to fall once the ball starts reversing.
